verses.95:1: Cantai ao Senhor um cântico novo: * cantai ao Senhor, toda a terra.
verses.95:2: Cantai ao Senhor, e {benedicite}: * anunciai de dia em dia a sua salvação.
verses.95:3: Anunciai entre as nações a sua glória, * entre todos os povos as suas maravilhas.
verses.95:4: Porque grande é o Senhor, e muito digno de louvor: * é terrível {super} todos os deuses.
verses.95:5: Porque todos os deuses das nações são {daemonia}: * o Senhor, porém, fez os céus.
verses.95:7: Trazei ao Senhor, ó {patriae} das nações, trazei ao Senhor glória e honra: * trazei ao Senhor glória ao seu nome.
verses.95:8: {tollite} vítimas, e entrai nos seus átrios: * adorai o Senhor no seu átrio santo.
verses.95:9: {commoveatur9} {afacie9} toda a terra: * dizei entre as {regnavit}.
verses.95:10: Pois ele {correxit} o mundo, que não será abalado: * julgará os povos com equidade.
verses.95:11: Alegrem-se os céus, e exulte a terra: {commoveatur11} o mar, e a sua plenitude: * os campos {gaudebunt}, e tudo o que neles há.
verses.95:12: Então exultarão todas as árvores das {silva} {afacie12}, porque vem: * porque vem julgar a terra.
verses.95:13: Julgará o mundo com equidade, * e os povos {veritate}.

decisions.why: The Latin has the dative (εὐλογήσατε τὸ ὄνομα, accusative in the Greek). The glossary row benedícere (man → God) keeps the Latin's case at no cost: accusative → *bendizei o*, dative → *bendizei ao*. Applied; MS1932's accusative is the option.

options.label: bendizei ao seu nome
options.note: draft — the row: the Latin's dative kept

options.label: bendizei o seu nome
options.note: MS1932; the everyday construction, the Greek's case

decisions.why: *super* here is rank (ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς θεούς; DRB 'above all gods'; MS1932 turns it into a comparative, *mais terrível que*). *sobre* is the Latin's word, but *terrível sobre* can be heard as 'terrible against / towards'; *acima de* says the rank plainly. The copula *é* is the Latin's own (*est*); the subject stays implied, carried from the first colon. Ps 94:3 (*Rex magnus super omnes deos*) and 96:9 (*super omnes deos*) are being or will be translated elsewhere; whichever word stands should be one in all three.

options.label: mais que
options.note: MS1932's comparative (*mais terrível que todos os deuses*) — it turns the preposition into a comparison

decisions.why: The Latin and the Greek say *demons* (δαιμόνια); the Hebrew says 'nothings / idols'. Rule 1: the Latin. *demônios* is DRB's 'devils' and MS1932's word, and the same word as 90:6 *o demônio do meio-dia*. The copula *são* is supplied (grammar).

options.label: demônios
options.note: draft — the Latin's word; MS1932, DRB

options.label: ídolos
options.note: the Hebrew's sense — refused under rule 1; shown so that the difference is visible

decisions.why: The noun *conféssio* is left open by D5 and the glossary names 95:6 as a place where *ação de graças* does not fit (what stands before God here is an attribute, beside beauty, not the people's thanks). ἐξομολόγησις is the noun of the verb D5 renders *dar graças*. *Louvor* (MS1932, DRB 'praise') is refused because this psalm spends *louvor* on *laudábilis* two verses earlier (95:4 *muito digno de louvor*) — two Latin roots would become one. *Confissão* keeps the Latin's word and its open range: the praise confessed and the sin confessed (the second is the reading an old commentator is remembered for — Augustine's 'Do you love beauty? Confess' — cited from memory, NOT verified). Its cost: a Brazilian hears the sacrament first. The nouns go without articles, as the Latin's two pairs do (a litany of attributes); MS1932 supplies them. Ruling: *Confissão*, for Gustavo's ear. 103:1 *Confessiónem et decórem induísti* is the twin and should decide with this.

options.label: Confissão
options.note: draft — the Latin's word; keeps both senses the Latin leaves open

options.label: Ação de graças
options.note: D5's family (dar graças); narrows to thanks, and the glossary itself says it does not fit here

options.label: Louvor
options.note: MS1932, DRB 'praise'; collides with laudábilis → digno de louvor in 95:4

options.label: A confissão e a beleza
options.note: the articles supplied in both colons, as MS1932

decisions.why: The glossary's *conspéctus* row is open: *à vista de* (Ps 5:9, 14:4a) or *na sua presença* (21:28b, 21:30, 49:3b — the same *in conspéctu ejus*). With a verbless copula (*estão*), *estão à vista dele* is heard as 'are visible to him'; *na sua presença* says where they stand. The Latin repeats *in … ejus* across the colons (*in conspéctu ejus … in sanctificatióne ejus*) and so does the Portuguese (*na sua presença … na sua santificação*).

options.label: à vista dele
options.note: the conspéctus row's proposal (5:9, 14:4a); keeps the seeing

decisions.why: ἐν τῷ ἁγιάσματι αὐτοῦ — the Greek word is the holy place, and DRB and MS1932 both say sanctuary. But the Latin chose *sanctificátio*, the act or state of hallowing, not *sanctuárium*; 77:54 already keeps it as *o monte da sua santificação* (the same Greek), so the Latin's word stands and the place is left for the ear to find. *sanctimónia* (ἁγιωσύνη, the Greek of 29:5 *sanctitátis* → *santidade*) takes *santidade* by D15's Greek test.

*pátria* here is not the fatherland but the clan: αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν, the same Greek as 21:28b *univérsæ famíliæ géntium* → *todas as famílias das nações* (read in consult/parallels/ps021.md). By D15's test the two Latin words share a Portuguese word. MS1932 *ó famílias das nações*, DRB 'kindreds of the Gentiles'. *ó* before the vocative as 28:1 *ó filhos de Deus*. The rest of the verse copies the formula of 28:2 (glossary row *Afférte Dómino*), as the row asks.

options.label: linhagens
options.note: keeps pátria apart from família; DRB 'kindreds'

decisions.why: ἄρατε θυσίας — the same Greek imperative as 23:7 *Attóllite portas* → *Erguei … as vossas portas*; by D15's test one Portuguese verb. It keeps the image of lifting the offering. MS1932 *Tomai vítimas*, but *tomar* already renders *súmere* in 80:3 *Súmite psalmum → Tomai um salmo* (λάβετε, another Greek verb). *Trazei* is refused: the Latin has just changed verbs (*afférte* → *tóllite*). *hóstia → vítima* (glossary row, open: the cognate is heard as the Host).

*commovéri → ser abalado* (glossary; one Greek, σαλεύω), and 95:10 *qui non commovébitur → que não será abalado* keeps the passive. The two jussives take the pronominal form of the same verb, *abale-se*: it is lighter than *seja abalada / seja abalado*, puts the verb first as the Latin does, and needs no gendered participle. The Latin says the same thing three times in three verses; so does the Portuguese. MS1932 *Trema … comova-se* are other verbs.

options.label: Estremeça
options.note: another verb (MS1932 *Trema*); breaks the psalm's threefold verb

decisions.latin: a fácie ejus … a fácie Dómini
decisions.why: ἀπὸ προσώπου / πρὸ προσώπου. The face is kept (rule 5; row *fácies*, and 17:43, 34:5, 41:3, 82:14 *diante da face de*). Both places the same, as the Latin. *da face dele* (the row *a fácie → da face de*, used after verbs of flight) would be heard here as the earth being shaken off his face. 95:12 runs about two syllables over the Latin with it; accepted. Ps 67 used *à face de* (shorter; *A terra foi abalada … à face do Deus do Sinai*, 67:9) — the option.

decisions.latin: dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit
decisions.why: The Latin's *quia* makes it reported speech; the Greek has none (εἴπατε … ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν, direct). Rule 1: the Latin → *que*. *Dóminus regnávit → o Senhor reinou* is the formula of 92:1a (glossary), the Latin's perfect (DRB 'hath reigned'); MS1932 has *reina*.

options.label: nações: O Senhor reinou
options.note: direct speech, the Greek's build; the formula heard whole

decisions.why: *corrígere → corrigir* (glossary row *corrípere* names 95:10 for it; 17:36b). Lewis & Short: 'to make straight, set right, bring into order', mostly 'to amend'; the Greek κατώρθωσεν is 'set upright, establish'. *corrigiu* keeps the Latin's word and its moral overtone; its cost is that the ear hears 'amended' before 'set straight'. *endireitou* is the literal image, but *endireitar* is held for *dirígere* (D22). *firmou* (MS1932) is *firmáre*'s, and 92:1b has that verb in this very phrase (*Pois ele firmou o mundo, que não será abalado*) — the two psalms differ in the Latin at exactly this word, so they differ here. *Pois ele* as 92:1b (étenim row; the subject named). *orbis terræ → o mundo* (D30).

options.label: endireitou
options.note: the root image and the Greek's; collides with dirígere (D22)

options.label: firmou
options.note: MS1932; firmáre's (92:1b) — would erase the difference between the two psalms

decisions.why: One verse has three verbs of joy: *læténtur* (εὐφραινέσθωσαν) → *alegrem-se*, *exsúltet* (ἀγαλλιάσθω) → *exulte*, *gaudébunt* (χαρήσεται) → a third word, because the Greek is a third verb too (D15's test). *regozijar-se* is free (the gáudium row lists *regozijo* as unused). MS1932 has *alegrar-se-ão*, which merges it with *lætári* two cola earlier. The subject first, then the verb (*os campos se regozijarão*): natural order, no mesóclise.

options.label: se regozijarão
options.note: draft — a third verb for a third Latin (and Greek) verb

decisions.why: *lignum → árvore* (glossary, open; 1:3 — it names 95:12) and *silva → selva* (D44; MS1932 *árvores das selvas*, word for word). Two readers have heard *selva* as jungle (73:6, 82:15), and the row is flagged for the coordinator; applied as settled until it is ruled.

options.label: matas
options.note: the everyday word; the stylist's at 73:6

decisions.why: *sua* is reflexive: the truth is the judge's. *na sua verdade* after *os povos* can be heard as the peoples' own truth; *dele* would fix it at the cost of an awkward cadence. *in veritáte → na … verdade* is the glossary's form (53:7 *na vossa verdade*); MS1932 *segundo a sua verdade* interprets the preposition. Kept the plain form for the readers to test. 9:8b (*julgará o mundo com equidade*) is copied in the first colon.

choices.95:1: *cantáre → cantar*, *cánticum novum → cântico novo* as 32:3, 39:4. The vocative *omnis terra → toda a terra* without *ó*, as the Latin.
choices.95:2: *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41), *de die in diem → de dia em dia* (row, 60:9), *salutáre → salvação* (D6).
choices.95:3: The second colon has no verb, as the Latin; *anunciai … entre as nações* as 9:12. *mirabília → maravilhas*.
choices.95:4: The first colon is the formula of 47:2 (*Grande é o Senhor, e muito digno de louvor*, settled D43), with *Porque* for *Quóniam*.
choices.95:5: *Dóminus autem → o Senhor, porém,* (26:10's placing of *autem*).
choices.95:6: *pulchritúdo → beleza* (row decor: kept apart from *esplendor* for exactly this verse and 103:1); *sanctimónia → santidade* (ἁγιωσύνη = 29:5 *sanctitátis*); *magnificéntia → magnificência* (row, open; unknown to two blind readers, kept).
choices.95:7: Copies the formula of 28:1–2 (*Trazei ao Senhor … glória e honra … trazei ao Senhor glória ao seu nome*) as the glossary row asks.
choices.95:8: The second colon copies 28:2 (*adorai o Senhor no seu átrio santo*), word for word as the Latin; *átrio* is the Latin's word (unknown to three blind readers, kept by the row). *introíte → entrai* (safe: *entrai* ≠ *entrei*).
choices.95:12: *quia venit … quóniam venit → porque vem … porque vem*: the Latin varies the conjunction, the Greek repeats ὅτι; the doubled *porque vem* is the psalm's climax and is kept. *exsultáre → exultar*.
choices.95:13: First colon = 9:8b *julgará o mundo com equidade* (twin, D30). *æquitas → equidade* (row; 66:5 *julgais os povos com equidade* is 95:10's second colon).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps095.md (no Diurnal section for this psalm) and the glossary. Formulas copied: 28:1–2 (95:7), 28:2 (95:8b), 47:2 (95:4a), 92:1a *o Senhor reinou* (95:9), 92:1b *Pois ele … o mundo, que não será abalado* (95:10a), 9:8b (95:13a). Hard readings: *conféssio* (open noun, D5), *sanctificátio* (sanctuary in the Greek), *corréxit* (against 92:1b *firmávit*), *tóllite* (Greek = 23:7). Words decided by D15's Greek test: pátriæ = famíliæ (21:28b), sanctimónia = sanctitas (29:5), tóllere = attóllere (23:7), gaudére ≠ lætári.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 95:6b −4 and 95:8 −5/−3 (Latin polysyllables — sanctificatióne, introíte, átria — against short Portuguese words; each colon still one breath, nothing to add that the Latin has); 95:11b +3 (*se regozijarão*, the third verb of joy — see gaudebunt); 95:12 +3/−3 (the face kept, *diante da face do Senhor*; *à face* is the shorter option); rhyme *equidade / verdade* in 95:13 — the Latin has the same echo (*æquitáte / veritáte*), so it stays.
